chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Sulayman ibn Umar who said: 'Imran ibn 'Ata narrated to me from 'Ata from Ibn Abbas from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said:

There is no word of speech more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than the statement 'La ilaha illallah'. And there is no servant who says 'La ilaha illallah' and prolongs his voice with it until he finishes, except that his sins fall scattered beneath his feet just as the leaves of a tree scatter beneath it.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: The declaration of monotheism (La ilaha illallah)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting La ilaha illallah loudly?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the spiritual efficacy of vocalizing the Shahada with prolongation (*mudd*), linking it to the immediate shedding of sins. The imagery of sins scattering like leaves underscores the completeness of divine forgiveness for this specific act of devotion, a theme frequently cited in Shia devotional practices to encourage loud dhikr.
